figures.definition_text: ₹10 crore if cash receipts and cash payments are each within 5% of the total, else ₹1 crore (s.44AB(a) and its proviso).

s.44AB(a): 'yes' when turnover certainly exceeds the applicable threshold however the cash share resolves, 'no' when it certainly does not, else 'undetermined'. This call: turnover is between the two possible thresholds; books cash share is within 5% on both legs, but a books-only breakdown can UNDERSTATE the true cash share (a non-account-payee cheque/draft counts as cash but is not visible in Tally as such -- a limit of 'Cash share of receipts and payments'); if the true share is not within 5%, the threshold reverts to ₹1 crore and turnover already exceeds it, so this cannot be asserted as a confident 'no'.

findings.title_text: s.44AB(e)/s.44AD(4)/(5) presumptive-taxation opt-out history not supplied
limits_text: Presumptive-taxation history was not supplied for this engagement; this test never assumes no opt-out occurred merely because the history is absent.
ask_client_text: For every year in the applicable s.44AD(4)/(5) lookback window: did the assessee declare income under s.44AD, and did it opt out (declare below the presumptive rate, or not under s.44AD at all) in any of those years while otherwise eligible? An opt-out can require an audit under s.44AB(e) independently of the turnover threshold above.

findings.title_text: s.44AB(b): a profession's tax audit turns on its gross receipts, which this test does not compute
limits_text: Whether the client carries on a profession is not recorded, and s.44AB(a) does not already require an audit here. s.44AB(b) requires a tax audit where gross receipts in a profession exceed ₹50 lakh in the previous year. A profession's gross receipts are not computed here. The CA determines.
